summary: This figure shows PICACHU's overall hardware architecture: a systolic array system and the pluggable PICACHU CGRA, both loosely coupled to a CPU that issues accelerator commands and receives responses. The systolic array holds Weight and Input Buffers feeding a MAC grid fed from DRAM, and its output passes through a Shared Buffer to the CGRA for nonlinear post-processing. The CGRA itself is a 4x4 mesh of 16 heterogeneous tiles of three types - Basic Tile (BaT), Branch-optimized Tile (BrT) and Compute Tile (CoT) - each with distinct functional units, shown color-coded in the mesh. Zoomed insets on the right detail the Precision-Aware FUs: a Vector Adder and Vector Multiplier that compose narrow bit-width operations (e.g. four 16-bit adds into two 32-bit adds) into wider results, plus a generic tile datapath with a configuration memory, register file and an 8x9 operand crossbar.
summary_zh: 该图展示 PICACHU 硬件架构：CPU 松耦合控制脉动阵列与可插拔 CGRA；阵列输出经共享缓冲送入由 BaT、BrT、CoT 三类瓦片构成的 4x4 CGRA 网格，右侧放大展示精度感知加法器/乘法器等功能单元。
